topics.topic: Explicit module_internal entries for the four model_items consumers
questions: Which four literal consumer keys must replace `<caller>`, and is this State 3 decision an enforceable obligation on State 5 despite the handoff declaring that nothing is carried further?

Replace the `<caller>` placeholder with explicit `module_internal` entries for `operations`, `owner_sessions`, `service_api` and `owner_interface`, each mapping `model_fields` to exactly `["model_items"]`.
Replace the `<caller>` placeholder with explicit entries for `operations`, `owner_sessions`, `service_api`, and `owner_interface`, using their exact `module_functions` keys.

quotes:
The walk of
a model is declared the same way (owner, 2026-11-26):
`module_internal["operations"]["model_fields"]`,
`module_internal["owner_sessions"]["model_fields"]`,
`module_internal["service_api"]["model_fields"]` and
`module_internal["owner_interface"]["model_fields"]` each hold
`model_items` alone, and `imports.internal["model_fields"]` exports it.
judgement.why: State 5 explicitly replaces the placeholder with the four literal consumer keys and fixes each import surface to model_items alone.

topics.topic: Scope of the prohibition on BaseModel imports, especially for models
questions: Does “no other module imports it” exclude the `models` module that must define classes which are instances of `BaseModel`, or does it prohibit only this exact import statement outside `model_fields`?
Does “no other module” include the `models` module that defines values which must be instances of `BaseModel`, or does it mean only that none of the four generic-walk callers imports `BaseModel`?
How does the `models` module define model classes that are instances of `BaseModel` while the text forbids every module other than `model_fields` from importing it?

quotes:
A model is any
instance of pydantic's base model class, which every model of `models` is;
`model_items` tells no class of models apart from another, and answers
`None` for every value that is no such instance.

`models`, whose models are the values it reads. It imports pydantic's base
model class as the third-party import `from pydantic import BaseModel`,
declared as `imports.third_party_by_module["model_fields"]`; no other module
imports it.
judgement.why: No witness is available because the texts require models to be BaseModel instances but never require the models module to bind BaseModel directly or state the alternative mechanism by which those classes are defined.

topics.topic: Whether model_fields directly depends on models and which symbols it imports
questions: Does `model_fields` have a direct dependency edge to `models`; if so, which exact exported model symbols does it import, given that its stated runtime check names only `BaseModel`?

Does `model_fields` have a runtime dependency edge to `models`; if so, which symbols owned by `models` does it directly import, given that it distinguishes values only through `BaseModel` and names no model class?
Does `model_fields` have a direct runtime dependency on `models`, and if so, which exact exported symbols does it import?

quotes:

judgement.why: The Knows entry declares models as a dependency even though the stated implementation directly imports only BaseModel from pydantic and names no models-owned symbol, for which the standard requires the models edge to be absent.

Reading the declared fields of a model value — each field's name and value,
in the order the model declares them — and telling a model from any other
value (owner, 2026-11-26; "Reading a model's fields").

author_guidance: Before editing, identify the decision's owning state from the phase purpose, question_scope and layer obligations, then choose a disposition for each topic that awaits one.
fixed: repair a decision the owning state must make; do not add later-layer implementation choices merely to close a topic. Record the fix commit and review the changed text once.

carried: name the receiving layer and use --what to preserve the choice, its options and consequences, and the required guarantee every option must keep. Decide any guarantee owned here before carrying its execution onward.
accepted: explain why the remaining choice is permitted. Bring an unresolved product choice to the owner with its options and consequences; absence of a quoted requirement does not decide it.
contradiction and standard_violation take no disposition: repair the offending text in its owning state and review the change. Deterministic transition findings must also close through their checks.
